translations.translatedText: # Wednesday 1.11.2017 (radio)

New York police have given more information about Tuesday's terrorist attack. The bosses of the game company Supercell earned the most in Finland last year. It rained a lot in October. The Finnish school in Texas congratulates Finland on its 100th birthday.
## The New York terrorist attack
![Authorities examine the car used in the terrorist attack in New York on 31 October.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9910293)
Open image viewer
Police examine the place in New York where a terrorist attack was carried out. Photo: Jason Szenes / EPA
New York police have given more information about Tuesday's terrorist attack. 8 people died in the attack.
The attacker was a 29-year-old man. He rented a car and drove it into people in Manhattan.
The police have found several knives in the man's car. There was also a piece of paper in the car saying that the man carried out the attack in the name of the terrorist organisation ISIS.
The police say that the man planned the act for many months. The man is now in hospital, because the police shot him.
The man was a driver for the ride company Uber. He comes from Uzbekistan. He moved to the USA in 2010.
## The highest pay
![Ilkka Paananen.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9910643)
Open image viewer
Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen got more than 46 million euros in pay last year. Photo: Yle
Last year's tax information was published on Wednesday. The tax information shows how much pay and other income people get.
The bosses of the game company Supercell had the most income.
The highest pay went to Supercell's Ilkka Paananen. He earned more than 46 million euros.
The second highest pay went to Mikko Kodisoja, and the third highest to John Derome. They are also Supercell bosses.
Derome earned more than anyone else last year when, for example, income from shares is counted in addition to pay. Derome's income was 74 million euros in total.
## A rainy October
![a yellow maple leaf in a puddle](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9884282)
Open image viewer
The autumn has been rainy. Photo: Jens Schlueter / EPA
It rained a lot in October.
The Finnish Meteorological Institute says that about 226 millimetres of rain fell in Nuuksio in Espoo. That is only 2 millimetres less than the October rain record.
October was really rainy in the south in particular. For example, it rained a lot in Uusimaa and Åland.
It was drier in the north. For example, in Nuorgam in Utsjoki, only a little over 10 millimetres of rain fell.
## Greetings from Texas
![A woman wearing a Finland shirt.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9910954)
Open image viewer
Pupils of the Finnish school in Texas. Photo: Yle
The Finnish schools' congratulations to Finland on its 100th birthday continue.
A large number of Finnish children and young people live in different parts of the world and study the Finnish language and Finnish culture in Finnish schools.
The Finnish schools are sending greetings to Finland on video, now that independent Finland turns 100.
The newest greetings and congratulations come from Dallas in the USA, from the Finnish school in Texas.
You can watch the greetings from the Finnish school in Texas on the Clear News website at yle.fi/selkouutiset, in the Finland 100 section.
The greetings can also be found on the Clear News Facebook page.
